items.title: Section: Confinement to a Realm, Explained Two Ways — By Where It Arises, and By Whether Pliancy Accompanies It

items.zh: 答：於此間生，未得對治；或得已出，三時現行義。一切一分是欲界繫。問：何義、幾蘊是色界繫？答：已得色界繫對治，若入彼定；或復生彼，未得上對治；或得已出，三時現行義。一切一分是色界繫。問：何義、幾蘊是無色界繫？答：已得無色界繫對治，若入彼定；或復生彼，未得上對治；或得已出，三時現行義。一切一分是無色界繫。復有差別。謂輕安俱三摩地及彼眷屬并彼果法所不攝義，是欲界繫。屬色煩惱、與彼相違所攝義，是色界繫。離色煩惱、彼所攝義，當知是無色界繫。
items.en: Answer: born here without yet possessing the antidote, or having attained and emerged from it, manifesting across the three times — a portion of all five is confined to the desire realm. Answer: having attained and entered the form-realm antidote, or born there without the higher antidote, or having attained and emerged from it — a portion is confined to the form realm. Answer: analogously for the formless realm. There is also a further distinction: whatever is not subsumed under pliancy-accompanied concentration and its own supporting factors and fruits is confined to the desire realm; what belongs to form-realm affliction is confined to the form realm; what is free of form-realm affliction yet still belongs to formless-realm affliction is confined to the formless realm.

items.title: Section: Wholesome, Unwholesome, Neutral — Explained Twice, Once by Result and Once by Fault

items.zh: 答：能感當來樂果報義，及煩惱苦永斷對治義。一切一分是善。問：何義、幾蘊是不善？答：能感當來苦果報義，及能發起諸惡行義。一切一分是不善。問：何義、幾蘊是無記？答：彼俱相違義。一切一分是無記。復有差別。謂離過失義，及過失功德對治隨順義，是善；與此相違義，是不善；彼俱相違義，是無記。
items.en: Answer: securing a pleasant future result, and permanently countering and severing affliction and suffering — a portion of all five is wholesome. Answer: securing a painful future result and giving rise to unwholesome conduct — a portion is unwholesome. Answer: neither of these — a portion is neutral. There is a further distinction: freedom from fault, together with countering fault and according with virtue, is wholesome; the opposite is unwholesome; neither is neutral.

items.zh: 問：何義、幾蘊是學？答：學方便善義。一切一分是學。問：何義、幾蘊是無學？答：學究竟善義。一切一分是無學。問：何義、幾蘊是非學非無學？

items.title: Section: Neither Learner Nor Beyond, Severed by Insight or Cultivation — Closing the Twenty-Nine Angles

items.zh: 答：離前二種所有善、染污、無記法義。一切一分是非學非無學。問：何義、幾蘊是見所斷？答：現觀智諦現觀所應斷義。一切一分是見所斷。問：何義、幾蘊是修所斷？答：從現觀後修道所斷義。一切一分是修所斷。問：何義、幾蘊是無斷？答：一切染污永斷對治義及已斷義。一切一分是無斷。問：何義、幾蘊是無色等？答：如前所說色等相違義，當知是無色等義。如是等類，應當分別諸蘊差別。
items.en: Answer: falling outside both learning and its completion — a portion is neither. Answer: what direct realisation at the initial stage of awakening cuts — a portion is severed by insight. Answer: what sustained cultivation following that realisation cuts — a portion is severed by cultivation. Answer: serving as the antidote that permanently severs all defilement, and having already been severed — a portion is beyond all severance. Answer: the opposite of what was said for being form and the rest should be understood as the meaning of being formless and the rest. Distinctions of this kind should be applied throughout to the aggregates.

items.title: Section: What "Aggregate" Actually Means — And Why a Noble One Feels Bodily Pain Without Mental Suffering

items.zh: 問：如說積聚義是蘊義，何等名為積聚義耶？答：種種所召體義、更互和雜轉義、一類總略義、增益損減義，是積聚義。
items.en:
Question: if aggregation is said to be the meaning of "aggregate," what constitutes aggregation? Answer: designating a collective entity, mutual intermixing, a single unified category, and increase and decrease — these constitute aggregation.
[From the Saṃyukta Āgama] Contemplate all form — past, future, present, internal, external, coarse, subtle, inferior, excellent, distant, or near — as neither self, nor different from self, nor mutually contained within self. So too for feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. An unlearned ordinary being, touched by painful sensation, generates two sensations — bodily and mental; a well-taught noble disciple, touched by painful sensation, generates only one — bodily, not mental.

items.title: Section: Why Form Is Called "Form" — Growth, and Two Kinds of Obstruction

items.zh: 問：何緣色蘊說名為色？答：於彼彼方所種殖增長義及變礙義，故名為色。此變礙義，復有二種。一、手等所觸便變壞義，二、方處差別種種相義。
items.en: Question: for what reason is form aggregate called "form"? Answer: being planted and growing in various locations, and alteration-and-obstruction, together give it this name. This alteration-and-obstruction is further of two kinds: alteration through direct contact, and distinction through occupied position.

items.title: Section: Why the Four Formless Aggregates Are Collectively Called "Name" — And Why the Mind Is Basically a Pile of Labels

items.zh: 問：何緣四無色蘊總說名名？答：順趣種種所緣境義，依言說名分別種種所緣境義，故說為名。
items.en: Question: for what reason are the four formless aggregates together called "name"? Answer: because they incline towards and engage whatever object is encountered, and because they depend on conventional designation to distinguish that same object — for these reasons, they are called "name."

items.title: Section: Each Aggregate Belongs to Its Own Nature Alone — And Opens the Meaning of Correspondence

items.zh: 問：諸蘊誰所攝？為何義故建立攝耶？答：自性所攝，非他性。為遍了知種種自類，是故建立。問：諸法誰相應？為何義故建立相應？
items.en: Question: to what do the aggregates belong, and for what purpose is subsumption established? Answer: each belongs to its own essential nature, never another's. It is established so that one may comprehensively understand each distinct category. Question: to what do phenomena correspond, and for what purpose is correspondence established?

items.title: Section: Anāthapiṇḍika's Deathbed Tears of Joy — Correspondence Closes the Aggregates' Entire Analysis

items.zh: 答：他性相應，非自性。為遍了知依自性清淨心，有染不染法若增若減，是故建立。
items.en: Answer: correspondence occurs with another nature, never with one's own. It is established so that one may fully understand mind's own inherently pure nature, appearing more or less defiled depending on what accompanies it. [From the story of Anāthapiṇḍika's final days] Ānanda asked: are your hands and feet you? The householder answered: no. Ānanda said: nor are form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness you. Hearing this, the householder wept, explaining it was not grief but joy, and asked that this same teaching be given to lay householders as well, not reserved only for the dying.

items.title: Section: Refuting "Only Mind Is Real" — Why Feeling, Perception, and Formations Cannot Be Mere Illusions

items.zh: 有一沙門、若婆羅門，欲令名中唯心實有，非諸心所。此不應理。何以故？且說諸蘊有五種性不成就故。又若彼計分位別故有五性者，分位別計，亦有過失。何以故？是諸分位展轉相望，作用差別若有若無，皆成失故。若言有者，由相異故，便應有異實物體性；若言無者，計分位別則為唐捐。
items.en: There are renunciants and brahmins who hold that within the name-aggregates, mind alone is genuinely real, not the mental factors. This is unreasonable. Why? Because it fails to establish the aggregates' own fivefold nature. If it is instead claimed that these five are established through mere positional difference, this too carries faults. Why? Because whether or not these positions display distinct function, both alternatives fail. If they display distinct function, their differing character demands separately real substances; if they display no distinct function, positing positional difference accomplishes nothing.

items.title: Section: Milk Curdling Into Yogurt — Why Mind Cannot Gradually Become Feeling, Perception, or Will

items.zh: 又不應謂如六識身分位差別。何以故？由六識身所依、所緣有差別故。是諸分位一處可得，故不應理。若謂轉變，亦不應理。何以故？於有色物可轉變故，得有分位前後差別，非於無色有如乳、酪、生酥等異。又心因緣無差別故，行別分位不應道理。於一剎那，必不可得差別因緣，令彼分位而有差別。
items.en: Nor should it be said these are positional phases like the six consciousnesses, since the six consciousnesses differ according to distinct supporting faculties and objects, while these positions all arise from the very same faculty and object at once — this is unreasonable. Nor should it be said they arise through gradual transformation, since only material things, capable of change, admit positional succession, unlike formless mind, which has nothing comparable to milk becoming yogurt or fresh butter. Nor is this reasonable given the causal condition generating mind shows no internal difference at all, since within a single instant, no differentiated cause can ever be found to account for positional difference.

items.zh: 是故汝計分位差別，不應道理。

blocks.text: Day 500. The twenty-nine angles end, and then a careful refutation of the view that only the mind itself is real and its factors are mere phases of it.
By birth without the antidote, or by not being included in absorption with pliancy.
Master Cháng Bǎi: contaminated good brings desirable results; uncontaminated good counters and permanently severs affliction and suffering.
Supramundane things are pure by nature and never to be severed. (Untranslated, 0608c05: the learner's aggregates are good as means to training; the arhat's, good as its completion.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: every form is a mixture of form, smell, taste, and touch, and every mind of four aggregates; "aggregate" is a collective name.
Growth in places and change-obstruction. Master Cháng Bǎi: struck by hand or stick, the faculties and objects change and break.
They incline towards objects and rely on names to distinguish them. Master Cháng Bǎi: to know anything, we need its name.
Master Cháng Bǎi: of one's own nature one says "included"; with another nature one says "corresponding". Mind's neutrality is its essential purity, not the severing of affliction.

If only mind were real and the factors mere positions of it, the fivefold nature of the aggregates would fail. Master Cháng Bǎi: this refutes those who hold that only the mind-king exists. (Untranslated, 0609a27: the sūtra calling "the six elements" a person has a hidden intent: it names the chief bases of form, movement, and mind.)
Only material things change through stages like milk, yogurt, and butter. Master Cháng Bǎi: a moment of mind ceases as it arises; it cannot slowly become feeling.
Five hundred days. The analysis is long, but its aim is simple: to see that what we call "me" is many things working together, none of which is a self.

quiz.q: What are the two accounts of being confined to the desire realm?
options: born here one is always so confined, absorption or not; and whatever has affliction is so confined, the higher realms included
having sexes; having food
not having taken precepts; not having heard the Dharma
born here without the antidote or having left it, active in three times; not subsumed under absorption with pliancy, its retinue, and fruits
quiz.why: The treatise gives two accounts: by birth without the antidote, or by what is not subsumed under absorption with pliancy, its accompanying factors, and result-form. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first is aggregates born in the desire realm not yet countered by absorption or the path; absorption with pliancy spans the preliminary concentration through the fourth absorption.

quiz.q: The English has "affliction's own suffering" for 煩惱苦. What is the problem?
options: 煩惱苦 is the suffering affliction brings, one thing, so the possessive is exact and needs no change
煩惱苦 is another name for painful feeling
煩惱苦 is the suffering of hell
煩惱苦 is two things, affliction and suffering; the English wrongly makes a possessive; the lecture says uncontaminated good severs affliction and suffering
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: contaminated good that brings desirable future results, and uncontaminated good that counters and permanently severs affliction and suffering, are called wholesome. So 煩惱苦 lists two things. The English "affliction's own suffering" makes a single thing and loses the point that the path ends both cause and result.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the second account of the wholesome?
options: fault and merit are the same, good and evil being mere discrimination, so the second account says there is no difference to choose between
only the uncontaminated is good, and all contaminated is bad
contaminated good accords with countering fault and leads to uncontaminated merit; the reverse, following fault and leaving merit, is unwholesome
only buddhas have wholesome phenomena
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: contaminated good accords with countering fault and has the merit of leading to uncontaminated good; what is opposed to good has fault, follows fault, and leaves merit. The English "countering fault and according with virtue" clearly unpacks the compact Chinese.

quiz.q: "Beyond all severance": the English has "what has been permanently countered and eliminated." Which sense is lost?
options: only one sense, an arhat's severed afflictions, so the English is right and learners' supramundane phenomena are excluded
two senses: the remedy that severs, supramundane phenomena, and what is already severed; the English keeps only the passive one, and it is not arhats alone
the Chinese says wholesome phenomena must be severed
the Chinese says nothing need be severed
quiz.why: The Sub-commentary gives two senses: supramundane phenomena, pure by nature at all times, are not to be severed; and other worldly phenomena are not to be severed because the severing is already done. Master Cháng Bǎi illustrates the latter with an arhat. The English keeps only what has been eliminated, losing the active remedy, which includes a learner's supramundane phenomena.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the four meanings of aggregation?
options: the aggregate is a provisional collective name; form and mind are intermixtures; many phenomena summed as one class
aggregation piles up many real small things, the form aggregate being a real heap, so aggregates are real, as the treatise holds
aggregation is accumulating merit
aggregation is storing goods
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the collective entity is a provisionally established collective name; every form is an intermixture of form, smell, taste, and touch, and every mind of four aggregates, so nothing stands alone; many phenomena in a class are summarised as one. The English "designating a collective entity" conveys the first.

quiz.q: Why is form called form, and what are the two kinds of obstruction?
options: form means colour; blue and yellow, since only the eye sees form, obstruction being a difference of two colours
growth in locations and obstruction; altered by contact of the hand and the like, and distinct by occupied position
form means beauty; beauty and ugliness
form means desire; male and female
quiz.why: The treatise gives growth in places and change-obstruction, the latter of two kinds. Master Cháng Bǎi: the five faculties and four objects change and break when struck by hand, foot, or stick; and differences of size and occupied place make them obstruct one another. The English "obstruction" leaves out 變, change, and "growth" leaves out 種植.

quiz.q: Why are the four formless aggregates together called name?
options: they incline towards various objects, and depend on designation to distinguish them
because they have no names, they are ironically called name, a mere agreed usage with no reason behind it
because they are all written words
because they make one famous
quiz.why: The treatise gives two reasons: they incline towards objects, and they rely on verbal designation to distinguish objects. Master Cháng Bǎi: to know any phenomenon we need its name; feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness can incline towards objects and, relying on names, make distinctions; and the name itself has no real substance.

quiz.q: "Subsumed by own nature, not another's": why establish subsumption, and what benefit does Master Cháng Bǎi see?
options: to add to the list of doctrines and make the treatise complete, with no direct benefit for practice, being mere scholarship
for ease of memorising
to know each class; observing subsumption breaks the mark of a heap, entering the gate of emptiness
for debating with outsiders
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: each aggregate stands for a nature proper to itself and not shared with others. Observing what the aggregates subsume, one comprehensively knows each class, breaks the mark of a heap, and so enters the gate of emptiness. So this classification is a contemplation, not mere bookkeeping.

quiz.q: What is the difference between subsumption and correspondence?
options: another nature is subsumption and own nature correspondence, since a phenomenon can correspond only to itself
they are the same, both classification
subsumption concerns form; correspondence nirvāṇa
own nature is subsumption; another nature is correspondence
quiz.why: The treatise says correspondence occurs with another nature, never with one's own. Master Cháng Bǎi: speaking of own nature one says subsumed, speaking of another nature one says corresponding. A practitioner should know it is mind joining defiled or undefiled phenomena, and not an "I" being defiled or not.

quiz.q: The English has "mind's own inherently pure nature, appearing more or less defiled." How does the subject differ?
options: what increases and decreases are defiled and undefiled phenomena, mind itself being neutral; the English has mind appearing more or less defiled
what increases is the pure mind itself, practice adding to its purity, so the English is exact and mind grows purer
what increases and decreases is lifespan
what increases is buddha-nature, omitted by the English
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: mind being neutral by nature is its essential purity, not that afflictions have been severed; it does not mean the merits of the fruit, and wisdom comes from infusion by hearing, not from being innate. In the Chinese what grows and declines is defiled and undefiled phenomena. The English "appearing more or less defiled" shifts this onto mind.

quiz.q: What is the treatise's first objection to "mind alone is real, not the mental factors"?
options: it violates common sense, all knowing that minds are many, so no reasoning is needed beyond what people think
it violates royal law
the aggregates' fivefold nature fails, leaving only form and mind
it would send one to hell
quiz.why: The treatise's first point is that the fivefold nature of the aggregates would fail. Master Cháng Bǎi: this refutes those who hold that only the mind-king exists; if mind alone were real and factors not, provisional phenomena having no substance, there would be only two aggregates, form and mind. This is not the Mahāyāna "mind-only."

quiz.q: If the five are said to be positional difference, how does the treatise refute this, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: positional difference is correct, the treatise agreeing and only faulting its clarity, and finally accepting it
if functions differ, separate substances follow; if not, the theory is pointless; mind and the others differ in function, so also in substance
because positional difference is an outsiders' term
because only form has phases, unrelated to function
quiz.why: The treatise argues by dilemma: if the positions differ in function, their differing character demands separate substances; if not, positing positional difference is pointless. Master Cháng Bǎi: in one moment the five aggregates function together, mind and the others differing in name and function; since they function differently, their substance should differ too.

quiz.q: Why can feeling and the like not be mind's transformation, as milk becomes yogurt?
options: only material things change through stages; the formless has nothing like milk and yogurt, and a moment of mind ceases at once
because milk cannot become yogurt, the simile itself being wrong, and the treatise points out that error
because mind is harder than milk
because yogurt is better than feeling and perception
quiz.why: The treatise says only material things can change through earlier and later stages; the formless has nothing like milk, yogurt, and butter. Master Cháng Bǎi: a present moment of mind ceases as it arises, so how could it stay to be transformed? The English "clarified butter" for 生酥 is questionable, since 生酥 comes before refined ghee in the usual series.
